findings.where: Article specimen, the numbered list under 'So, what are the key chapter topics?' (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The list numbers are set in the blue used for links, in the sans, next to grey serif text. The specimen's own note beside it says 'blue only where something can be clicked', but these numbers cannot be clicked. The sans numerals also look smaller and lighter than the serif text they introduce, so the number and its item don't read as one.
findings.who_objects: Someone reading Mark's article, who has just been told that blue means clickable and then sees blue numbers that do nothing. Angélique, too, would be passing on a rule that breaks itself the first time she adds a list.

findings.where: Article specimen, the title 'The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law'; also 'Mark's' in the type-pair copy and in the first-screen photo note
findings.fault: The apostrophe at display size is a straight typewriter mark. Elsewhere the page uses curly quotes (‘chapter topics’, ‘Abundance’, “Not yet!”, and Mark’s in the footer and the article caption), so the same mark is set two ways, and the straight one sits in the biggest type in the article.
findings.who_objects: A reader used to legal journals and bank publications, and Mark himself, a lawyer: in a large serif headline a straight apostrophe looks like an unedited draft and undercuts the serious, editorial tone the type is chosen for.

findings.where: Article specimen, the byline 'Mark M. Moseley · Blog No. 8 · 18 September 2024' under the title (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The byline sits almost touching the title's descenders, with less space above it than the gap between the title's own two lines. Below it there is a wide gap before the body. So the byline reads as squeezed onto the headline rather than as its own line of information.
findings.who_objects: A reader scanning for who wrote the piece and when: the date and author are cramped against the heading and easy to skip, and the page looks less carefully set than its 32 px rhythm claims.

findings.where: Article specimen, the lecture entry 'Streamlining the PPP Process: Meeting the ‘Abundance’ Challenge' with its PDF link (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The entry's title and date are set about 4 px in from the article's left edge, so they don't line up with the text column above. The title is set in the same size, weight and colour as the body text, on the body's loose 32 px line, so a two- or three-line title reads as stray paragraph text rather than the name of a document to download.
findings.who_objects: A bank or agency reader looking for Mark's papers, which the research calls the product: the entry doesn't read as a distinct item. The off-by-a-few-pixels edge also looks like a slip to anyone with an eye for setting.
